mainTopic: רבי יהודה's exemption of a סומא, the משנה on who pays for injuring a person, and who receives payment for injuring a young daughter
overview: The amud begins by finishing רבי יהודה's view on a סומא. He exempts a blind person from all civil laws, learned from the פסוק about the killer and the גואל הדם. A second ברייתא has him exempt a סומא from all מצוות, and רב שישא בריה דרב אידי links מצוות to משפטים through another פסוק. רב יוסף, who was blind, first wanted the הלכה to follow רבי יהודה. After hearing רבי חנינא say that one who is commanded and does is greater, he wanted the opposite. Then a new משנה teaches that a person who injures pays all five payments plus דמי ולדות, while an ox's owner pays only נזק. It goes through special cases: parents, יום הכפורים and שבת, Hebrew and Canaanite slaves, the חרש, שוטה וקטן, and the slave and married woman. The גמרא opens with רבי אלעזר asking רב who receives the payment when someone injures another man's young daughter. The question's two sides are laid out, and רב's answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה exempts a blind person from all civil laws
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that רבי יהודה exempted a סומא from all the civil laws of the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the same way, רבי יהודה used to exempt a blind person from all the civil laws in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא about a blind person: רבי יהודה exempted him from all the civil laws of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, the ברייתא was talking about one specific law that does not apply to a blind person. Now it widens the rule: according to רבי יהודה, a סומא is outside all of the civil laws.

keyTerms.meaning: exempts him
civil laws (the money and damages laws between people)
a blind person

phrases.english: And so Rabbi Yehuda would exempt him
phrases.notes: "Him" means the blind person the ברייתא was just talking about.

phrases.english: from all the civil laws that are in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה פּוֹטְרוֹ מִכׇּל דִּינִים שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from before this section about רבי יהודה's view on a סומא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a סומא is exempt from all the civil laws of the תורה.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה exempts a סומא from civil laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי יהודה's rule. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק will be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on רבי יהודה. It is a simple request: where in the תורה does this exemption come from?

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for exempting a סומא from civil laws.

steps.title: Learning it from the verse about the killer and the avenger
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links "these laws" to the killer and the גואל הדם. Whoever is outside that law is outside all civil laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "The congregation shall judge between the killer and the blood-avenger according to these laws." Whoever is included in the law of the killer and the blood-avenger is included in the civil laws. Whoever is not included in it is not included in the civil laws.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that ties the civil laws to the law of the accidental killer and the גואל הדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts "the killer and the גואל הדם" side by side with "these laws." רבי יהודה reads this as a link between the two. A סומא is not part of the killer law, so he is not part of the civil laws either.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who struck (here, the accidental killer)
the blood-avenger, a relative of the person killed
laws / civil judgments
the verse says

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק itself never mentions a blind person. The link comes from a separate rule (hinted in the note below): a blind person who kills by accident is not part of the killer law at all.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And the congregation shall judge
between the smiter and the blood-avenger
according to these laws".

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּמַכֶּה וּבְגוֹאֵל הַדָּם, יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּמִשְׁפָּטִים;
phrases.english: Whoever is included in the law of the smiter and the blood-avenger is included in the civil laws;
whoever is not included in the law of the smiter and the blood-avenger,
phrases.notes: A blind person fits here, because a blind accidental killer is not sent to exile ("בלא ראות", במדבר 35:23).

phrases.english: is not included in the civil laws.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְשָׁפְטוּ הָעֵדָה בֵּין הַמַּכֶּה וּבֵין גֹּאֵל הַדָּם
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links the civil laws to the killer and the גואל הדם. Whoever is outside that law is outside the civil laws.

steps.title: Another teaching: a blind person is exempt from all מצוות
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה. A סומא gets no payment for בושת, and he is exempt from all מצוות in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says a blind person does not receive payment for embarrassment. And so רבי יהודה would exempt him from all the מצוות stated in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא. In this one, רבי יהודה exempts a סומא from all the מצוות, not just from the civil laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא only spoke about civil laws. This one goes much further and includes every מצוה in the תורה. That is a far bigger claim, and the גמרא will need a new source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: another ברייתא teaches
payment for embarrassment
commandments

phrases.english: Another ברייתא teaches: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A blind person does not have payment for embarrassment.
And so Rabbi Yehuda would exempt him
from all the מצוות stated in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: סוֹמֵא אֵין לוֹ בּוֹשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא that widens רבי יהודה's exemption to all מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a סומא gets no בושת payment and is exempt from all מצוות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for רב יוסף's personal reaction in the next steps.

steps.title: רב שישא asks for the source of the wider exemption
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי asks what רבי יהודה's source is for exempting a סומא from all מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי said: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא asks for the source of this second, wider exemption. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The killer פסוק only explained the civil laws. The exemption from all מצוות needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: the son of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for exempting a סומא from all מצוות.

steps.title: Commandments are linked to civil laws
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק lists מצוות, חוקים and משפטים together. Whoever is outside the משפטים is outside the מצוות and חוקים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And these are the commandments, the statutes, and the laws." Whoever is included in the laws is included in the commandments and statutes. Whoever is not included in the laws is not included in the commandments and statutes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא answers with a פסוק that groups מצוות, חוקים and משפטים together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds a chain. Step 3 showed that a סומא is outside the משפטים. This פסוק links מצוות and חוקים to the משפטים. So a סומא is outside the מצוות and חוקים as well.

keyTerms.meaning: statutes (laws whose reason is not given)

steps.whatToRemember: There is a two-link chain. The killer law is tied to the civil laws (step 3), and the civil laws are tied to all מצוות (this step). A סומא is outside the first, so for רבי יהודה he is outside all of them.

phrases.english: The verse says: "And these are the commandments,
the statutes, and the laws".

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּמִשְׁפָּטִים, יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּמִצְוֹת וְחֻקִּים;
phrases.english: Whoever is included in the laws is included in the commandments and statutes;

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּמִשְׁפָּטִים, אֵינוֹ בְּמִצְוֹת וְחֻקִּים.
phrases.english: and whoever is not included in the laws is not included in the commandments and statutes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וְאֵלֶּה הַמִּצְוֹת הַחֻקִּים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by building on the exemption from משפטים shown in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links מצוות and חוקים to משפטים. Since a סומא is outside the משפטים, he is outside all מצוות.

steps.title: רב יוסף's first reaction: happy to be exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, who was blind, says that at first he would have made a celebration if the הלכה followed רבי יהודה. He kept the מצוות even though he was not commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: At first I would say: if someone told me the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who says a blind person is exempt from מצוות, I would make a celebration for the rabbis. Why? Because I am not commanded, and still I do מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tells how he first felt about רבי יהודה's ruling. He would have been glad, because it would mean his keeping of מצוות was extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His thinking was that doing a מצוה voluntarily, without being obligated, is more praiseworthy. So being exempt would make his מצוות worth more.

keyTerms.meaning: at first
a festive day (celebration) for the rabbis
I am commanded

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: At first I would say:
Whoever tells me the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
who says a blind person is exempt from the מצוות,
I would make a festive day for the rabbis.
What is the reason? Because I am not commanded,
and still I do מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a personal reaction to רבי יהודה's exemption of a סומא from מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף first thought that doing מצוות without being commanded is greater.

steps.title: רב יוסף changes his mind: being commanded is greater
steps.stepSummary: After hearing רבי חנינא say that one who is commanded and does is greater, רב יוסף now wants the הלכה to go against רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But now that I heard רבי חנינא's teaching, that one who is commanded and does a מצוה is greater than one who is not commanded and does it, if someone tells me the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה, I would make a celebration for the rabbis. Why? Because if I am commanded, I get more reward.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף reverses his first view. He now wants to be obligated, because of רבי חנינא's teaching that one who is commanded gets more reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא's rule turns step 7 upside down. Being obligated is not a loss. It raises the value of the מצוה. So רב יוסף now hopes the הלכה goes against רבי יהודה, which would make him commanded.

keyTerms.meaning: greater is one who is commanded and does
reward
more

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא's principle: one who is commanded and does a מצוה is greater than one who is not commanded and does it. רב יוסף's story shows him changing his mind because of it.
steps.confusionAlert: Both times רב יוסף says he would make a celebration, but for opposite news. First he wanted the הלכה to follow רבי יהודה. Now he wants it not to follow רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source for the idea that being obligated in a מצוה makes it more valuable.

phrases.english: But now that I heard this teaching of Rabbi Chanina,
as Rabbi Chanina said:
Greater is one who is commanded and does
than one who is not commanded and does;

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר לִי: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: whoever tells me the halacha does not follow Rabbi Yehuda,
I will make a festive day for the rabbis.
What is the reason? Because when I am commanded,
I have more reward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses רב יוסף's first view from step 7, based on רבי חנינא's teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One who is commanded and does a מצוה is greater than one who is not commanded. So רב יוסף prefers that the הלכה not follow רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A person who injures pays more than an ox
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens by contrasting the two. A person who injures pays all five payments plus דמי ולדות. An ox's owner pays only נזק and is exempt from דמי ולדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Here is a way a person is treated more strictly than an ox. A person pays for damage, pain, medical costs, lost work, and embarrassment. He also pays for unborn babies. An ox pays only for damage, and it is exempt from paying for unborn babies.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה begins. It lists what a person must pay for injuring someone, compared to what an ox's owner pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who injures owes five separate payments: נזק, צער, ריפוי, שבת and בושת. On top of that he owes דמי ולדות if he caused a miscarriage. An ox's owner owes only the basic נזק, so the person's list is much longer.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, meaning 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a new משנה.
A stringency, a way one case is treated more strictly.
The five payments for injury: damage, pain, medical costs, lost work time, and embarrassment.
Payment for unborn babies lost when a pregnant woman is struck and miscarries.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the five payments with דמי ולדות. The five are paid to the injured person. דמי ולדות is a separate payment for causing a miscarriage.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
This is a stringency with a person compared to an ox:
that the person pays for damage, pain,
medical costs, lost work time, and embarrassment,
and he pays the value of unborn babies;
but an ox pays only for damage,
and is exempt from the value of unborn babies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion of רבי יהודה and the סומא ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who injures pays all five payments plus דמי ולדות. An ox's owner pays only נזק and no דמי ולדות.

steps.title: Striking a parent without a wound, or injuring on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: Two cases might seem to be special: striking a parent without causing a wound, and injuring someone on יום הכפורים. In both, the injurer pays all five payments.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone hits his father or mother but does not make a bleeding wound, or injures another person on יום הכפורים, he must pay all five payments.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two cases where the injury is also a sin. It rules that the attacker still pays everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hitting a parent and causing a חבורה is a capital crime. The משנה is careful to speak about a case with no חבורה, where there is no death penalty. Injuring on יום הכפורים also carries no court death penalty. So in both cases nothing stops the regular payments, and the attacker is חייב בכולן.

keyTerms.meaning: A wound or bruise where blood gathers or comes out.
One who injures another person.
Liable for all of them, meaning all five payments.

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'without a wound' are not making the case lighter. They make sure there is no death penalty, and that is why money is owed.

phrases.english: One who strikes his father or his mother
and did not make a wound on them,
and one who injures his fellow on יום הכפורים,
is liable for all of them.
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all five payments listed just before.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּכֶּה אֶת אָבִיו וְאֶת אִמּוֹ וְלֹא עָשָׂה בָּהֶן חַבּוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the five payments from step 9 to cases where the injury is also a sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Striking a parent without a חבורה, or injuring on יום הכפורים, makes one liable for all five payments.

steps.title: Injuring a Hebrew slave
steps.stepSummary: Someone who injures an עבד עברי pays all five payments. The exception is שבת, lost work time, when the slave belongs to the injurer himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who injures a Hebrew slave pays all five payments. He does not pay for lost work time if the slave belongs to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to a Hebrew slave. It rules that he gets the full payments, except for one payment in one situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד עברי is still a free Jew in his body, so he gets every payment. His work time, though, belongs to his master. If the master is the one who injured him, the lost work is the master's own loss. So there is no one else to pay for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A Hebrew slave, a Jew sold into service for a limited time.
Except for.
At a time when he belongs to him, meaning the injurer is his master.

phrases.english: One who injures a Hebrew slave
is liable for all of them,
except for lost work time
at a time that he is his.
phrases.notes: He means the slave belongs to the very person who injured him, his own master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from special situations to a special kind of victim.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Injuring an עבד עברי makes one liable for all five payments, except שבת when the injurer is his own master.

steps.title: Injuring someone else's Canaanite slave, and רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says one who injures another person's עבד כנעני pays all five. רבי יהודה says slaves have no בושת, so that payment drops out.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who injures a Canaanite slave who belongs to someone else pays all five payments. רבי יהודה says: slaves have no embarrassment payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a ruling about a Canaanite slave. Then it brings רבי יהודה, who disagrees about one payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the first view, an עבד כנעני is fully covered, and the payments go to his owner. רבי יהודה takes away only בושת, so the injurer pays the other four. This is the same רבי יהודה who said in step 4 that a סומא gets no בושת.

keyTerms.meaning: A Canaanite slave, a non-Jewish slave owned permanently.
Belonging to others, meaning not to the one who injured him.
Slaves have no embarrassment payment.

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יהודה again limits בושת to certain people, just as he did with the סומא. Seeing this pattern helps you follow his opinion through the סוגיא.

phrases.english: One who injures a Canaanite slave belonging to others
is liable for all of them.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Slaves do not have embarrassment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the Hebrew slave to the Canaanite slave and adds a disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says all five payments apply. רבי יהודה says there is no בושת for slaves.

steps.title: Deaf-mute, mentally incompetent person, and minor: liability goes one way only
steps.stepSummary: Dealing with a חרש, שוטה or קטן is a bad deal. If you injure them, you pay. If they injure you, they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, and a minor are bad to run into. If someone injures them, he must pay. If they injure others, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to people who are not responsible for their actions. It shows that the liability runs only one way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These three are full victims, so anyone who injures them pays. They lack the understanding to be held responsible, so they owe nothing when they injure others. That is why meeting them is called פגיעתן רעה: you can only lose.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute, who cannot hear or speak.
A mentally incompetent person.
A minor, a child below the age of מצוות.
Running into them is bad, because you can only lose.
Exempt, they do not have to pay.

steps.whatToRemember: A person pays more than an ox: all five payments plus דמי ולדות. These payments still apply when the injury is also a sin, and to a Hebrew or Canaanite slave, with the exceptions noted. A חרש, שוטה וקטן receive payment but never pay.

phrases.english: A deaf-mute, an incompetent person, and a minor
meeting up with them is bad,
one who injures them is liable,
but they who injured others are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from special victims to people who are special both as victims and as injurers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who injures a חרש, שוטה or קטן is liable. They are exempt when they injure others.

steps.title: A slave and a married woman: exempt now, pay later
steps.stepSummary: Injuring a slave or a married woman makes you liable. If they injure others, they are exempt for now, but they must pay once the woman is divorced or the slave is freed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A slave and a married woman are bad to run into. If you injure them, you pay. If they injure you, they are exempt for now. They pay later, once the woman is divorced or the slave is freed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second 'bad deal' case, much like the חרש, שוטה and קטן in step 13. This time the exemption only lasts for a while.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חרש, שוטה and קטן are exempt because they are not responsible. The slave and the married woman are responsible, but right now they have no money of their own to pay with. So their debt only waits: once they become independent, the obligation becomes active.

keyTerms.meaning: Running into them is bad, meaning it is a losing situation for the other person
One who injures someone else
At a later time
She became divorced
He became freed (a slave set free)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the חרש, שוטה and קטן in step 13. They are fully exempt forever. The slave and the married woman are only exempt for now and must pay later.

phrases.english: A slave and a woman, an encounter with them is bad,
phrases.notes: The woman here is a married woman; while she is married she has no money of her own to pay with.

phrases.english: one who injures them is liable,
and if they injured others, they are exempt,
but they pay at a later time.
If the woman became divorced, or the slave became freed,
they are obligated to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 'bad deal' case of step 13 with a new pair, where the exemption is only temporary.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who injures a slave or a married woman is liable. When they injure others they are exempt for now, and they must pay after a divorce or after being freed.

steps.title: Wounding a parent or wounding on שבת: no payment
steps.stepSummary: One who strikes a parent and causes a wound, or who injures anyone on שבת, pays none of the five payments because he faces the death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone hits his father or mother and makes a wound, or injures someone on שבת, he does not pay any of the payments, because he is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives cases where the injurer pays nothing at all, because the act carries the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compare step 10. There, hitting a parent without a wound meant he paid all five payments. Here there is a wound, so the act carries the death penalty, and that removes the money payments. On שבת, making a wound is itself a forbidden act that carries the death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: One who strikes
A bruise or wound that breaks the skin or draws blood
On שבת
He is judged with his life, meaning he is liable to the death penalty

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general rule: when one act brings both the death penalty and a money payment, the money payment drops out.

phrases.english: One who strikes his father or his mother
and made a wound on them,
and one who injures his fellow on שבת,
is exempt from all of them,
because he is judged with his life.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּכֶּה אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ וְעָשָׂה בָּהֶן חַבּוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from temporary exemptions to full exemptions, and contrasts with step 10, where these same kinds of cases without a wound meant full payment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wounding a parent, or injuring anyone on שבת, frees the injurer from all five payments because he faces the death penalty.

steps.title: Injuring one's own Canaanite slave
steps.stepSummary: One who injures his own עבד כנעני pays none of the five payments.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone injures his own Canaanite slave, he does not pay any of the payments.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with one more case of full exemption: the slave belongs to the injurer himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, injuring someone else's עבד כנעני meant paying the payments to the owner. Here the injurer is the owner, so there is nobody else to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew
His own
Exempt from all of them, meaning all five payments

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with a full picture. Some people always pay, some are exempt forever (חרש, שוטה, קטן), some pay later (slave, married woman), and some pay nothing because of the death penalty or because the victim is their own slave.

phrases.english: And one who injures his own Canaanite slave
is exempt from all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final full exemption, the reverse of step 12, where the slave belonged to someone else.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An owner who injures his own עבד כנעני pays none of the five payments.

steps.title: Who gets paid for injuring someone else's young daughter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רבי אלעזר asking רב: when someone injures another man's minor daughter, who receives the payment for the injury?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked רב: if someone injures another person's young daughter, who gets the payment for the injury?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion with a question that רבי אלעזר brought to רב. This step only states the question. The next two steps lay out the two possible sides, and רב's answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father has certain rights to his young daughter's work. So it is unclear whether the injury payment belongs to the father or to the girl herself. The question asks who owns the payment, not whether the injurer must pay.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
He asked of him, used for raising a question that needs an answer
A minor daughter, a young girl
Injury, here meaning the payment for the injury

phrases.english: Gemara
Rabbi Elazar asked of Rav:
One who injures the minor daughter of others,
the injury payment goes to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה has ended, and the גמרא opens a new discussion with a question about who receives injury payments.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When someone injures another man's minor daughter, does the payment go to her father or to the girl herself?

steps.title: First side: the father gets the injury payment
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the injury payment belongs to the father. The תורה already gave him שבח נעורים, and the injury lowered her value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that since the Merciful One gave the father the profits of her youth, the injury payment also belongs to her father? Why? Because the injurer lowered her money value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain רבי אלעזר's question by laying out the first possible answer: the father collects the injury payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives a father the money benefits of his young daughter, called שבח נעורים. An injury makes her worth less, so the father gets less from her later. That suggests the injury payment should go to him too.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we say? This opens the first side of a question.
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
The profits of youth, the money benefits a father gets from his young daughter
Injury, and the payment for it
He lowered her money value

phrases.english: Do we say:
since the Merciful One granted
the profits of youth to the father,
phrases.notes: These are the money benefits the תורה gives a father from his young daughter, such as the money given for her קידושין.

phrases.english: the injury payment also belongs to her father?
What is the reason?
Because he lowered her money value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the question asked in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the father's right to שבח נעורים also give him the injury payment, since the injury lowered her value?

steps.title: Second side: the injury payment is not the father's
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe the father only gets שבח נעורים because he controls her marriage. He has no right to injure her, so the injury payment is not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the Merciful One gave him only the profits of her youth, since if he wants to marry her off to a man with boils, he can. But for injury, since he is not allowed to injure her, the Merciful One did not give him that payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second possible side: the father does not collect the injury payment. This completes רבי אלעזר's question, and רב's answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rights the תורה gives the father match the control he has over her. He may marry her off even to a מוכה שחין, so the profits of her youth are his. He has no power to injure her, so perhaps the injury payment does not belong to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This opens the second side of a question.
A man afflicted with boils, a very undesirable match
He is able, he has the power
Granted ownership, gave the rights to

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think side two says the father may hurt his daughter's interests however he likes. It says the opposite: since he may NOT injure her, the injury payment may not be his.
steps.whatToRemember: The question has two sides. (1) The father gets the injury payment because the injury lowered her value and hurt his שבח נעורים. (2) The father's rights depend on his power over her, and he has no power to injure her, so the payment is not his.

phrases.english: Or perhaps
